sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Constitutional Basis**: Enacted under **Article 253** (Legislation for giving effect to international agreements). It gives effect to the decisions taken at the **UN Conference on the Human Environment (Stockholm, 1972)**.
• **Umbrella Act**: It is called an 'Umbrella Act' because it provides a framework for the Central Government to coordinate the activities of various central and state authorities established under previous laws (e.g., Water Act, Air Act).
• **Delegated Legislation**: Section 3 empowers the Central Government to take all measures it deems necessary for protecting and improving the quality of the environment.
• **Key Metric**: The Act grants the Central Government the power to issue direct orders, including the power to close, prohibit, or regulate any industry, operation, or process.

items.definition: Any solid, liquid, or gaseous substance present in such concentration as may be, or tend to be, injurious to the environment.

Any substance or preparation which, by reason of its chemical or physico-chemical properties, is liable to cause harm to human beings, other living creatures, plants, microorganisms, property, or the environment.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **EIA Notification (1994/2006)**: Mandates environmental clearance for projects under the EPA.
• **CRZ Notification**: Regulates activities in coastal zones to protect fragile ecosystems.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Over-centralization, lack of public participation in decision-making, and weak enforcement mechanisms.
• **Solutions**: Strengthening the role of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) and integrating 'Polluter Pays Principle' more effectively.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'EPA-1986: S-3, S-5, S-15'
• **Decoded Meaning**: S-3 (Standards/Powers), S-5 (Stop/Closure), S-15 (Penalty/Cognizance of offences).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the EPA with the Wildlife Protection Act. Remember, EPA is an 'Umbrella Act' for pollution and industrial regulation, not for wildlife conservation.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Statutory Framework for Environmental Governance' when discussing the EPA in the context of sustainable development.

keyTakeaways: EPA 1986 is the primary legislation for environmental protection in India.
It provides the Central Government with sweeping powers to regulate industrial activities.
It serves as the legal basis for major environmental notifications like EIA and CRZ.
